summary:
AstroGuard is an AI-assisted health monitoring application designed to support astronaut well-being during space missions. Microgravity, radiation, sleep disruption, fatigue, and psychological stress can affect astronauts' health, making continuous monitoring essential.

The application records key health measurements, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, respiratory rate, and systolic blood pressure. It allows users to establish personal Earth-based baseline values and compare them with mission measurements. Its rule-based analysis module evaluates health data using predefined criteria, identifies potential deviations, and generates alerts.

AstroGuard also provides interactive graphs to visualize health trends, an SQLite database to store records, CSV export, and emergency and measurement guides.

Additionally, Google Gemini API powers an AI assistant that generates contextual responses using users' questions and relevant health data, helping them better understand their measurements.

By combining personalized monitoring, rule-based alerts, data visualization, and generative AI, AstroGuard aims to make astronaut health tracking more systematic and accessible. The prototype could be further developed through real-time sensor integration and validation for spaceflight environments.

# Detailed Project Description

## Overview of what the project does

A web based application that tracks astronauts health. This can measure various medical metrics and help identify any potential issues facing astronauts.

This application has a profile section where users can input information about specific astronauts. This can then allow individuals to input their personal medical metrics on Earth. During their mission in space they can then input their new metrics.

The application tracks many different health metrics such as heart rate, body temperature, oxygen levels, breathing rate, blood pressure, radiation exposure. Astroguard also tracks how long astronauts sleep for, how well they sleep, how much they exercise, how tired they are, their stress levels and any symptoms they may have.

The system will process the metrics that have been input and classify them into either normal, warning or critical. Graphs will show how their health metrics have changed over time. The application will also include an AI assistant, an emergency section and a mission control section.

## Benefits of the project

The primary benefit is having different health metrics for astronauts on one platform.
